decisions.reason: It extends the firm's wafer and substrate know-how and, given the firm's in-house R&D, management would expect to keep learning and improving it rather than exit quickly.
This carrier wafer is a close, incremental extension of the established handling and packaging offer, so absorptive capacity is high and the product is likely to stay.
As a flagship product that builds directly on the firm's core glass-wafer capabilities and benefits from its R&D base, it fits the knowledge base and strategic direction well.
The off-the-shelf glass and quartz wafer line is very close to the firm's established business and supports commercialization of existing know-how, making withdrawal unlikely.

Glass-based circuit boards are comparatively distant from the firm's narrow core substrate business, so despite its R&D capabilities management is less able to assimilate feedback and would be more likely to redeploy resources elsewhere.
